# context-cli

Install:

```
composer require rasuvaeff/context-cli
```

Requires `ext-pcntl`, `ext-posix` (no Windows) and `rasuvaeff/context` ^0.3.

## Rules

- SIGTERM/SIGINT (configurable) cancel a context derived from your parent via
  `withCancel()`; the code stops at its next check (`assertActive()`,
  `sleep()`, `iterate()`, `is*()`), never mid-call.
- The handler only calls `ContextController::requestCancel()`: no listener,
  no application code runs inside a signal handler.
- A second signal of the set restores the previous handlers and hands that
  signal to them (PHP handler called; default disposition terminates; ignored
  stays ignored) — Ctrl+C twice always stops the process.
- One process, one handler table: two active scopes on one signal →
  `LogicException`. `SIGKILL`/`SIGSTOP`/duplicates/empty → `InvalidArgumentException`.
- Always restore: use `run()` or `restore()` in `finally`. The scope enables
  `pcntl_async_signals(true)` and restores the previous mode.

## API

```php
use Rasuvaeff\Context\Cli\SignalReceived;
use Rasuvaeff\Context\Cli\SignalScope;
use Rasuvaeff\Context\Context;
use Rasuvaeff\Context\ContextCancelledException;

// run(): install, call, restore (also when $work throws); returns $work's result
$result = SignalScope::run(Context::background(), static function (Context $ctx): int {
    $done = 0;
    foreach ($ctx->iterate($jobs) as $job) { handle($job, $ctx); $done++; }
    return $done;
}, signals: [\SIGTERM, \SIGINT]);

// manual
$scope = SignalScope::listen(Context::background(), [\SIGTERM, \SIGINT, \SIGHUP]);
try { work($scope->context()); } finally { $scope->restore(); }   // restore() is idempotent
$scope->signal();                       // ?int: first signal received

try { $ctx->assertActive(); } catch (ContextCancelledException $e) {
    $e->getPrevious();                  // SignalReceived: ->signal() === SIGTERM, message "Received SIGTERM"
}
SignalReceived::name(\SIGTERM);         // "SIGTERM"; unknown → "signal 14"
```

Kubernetes/systemd: SIGTERM → grace period → SIGKILL; the longest step between
two checks must fit in the grace period.
